resources.string:
Focus Guard lets Intent show your pause screen even when an app you marked as mindful is opened from a notification or the recents screen, and end the sessions you chose (for example, 5 minutes of Instagram).

To do that it only learns which app is in front, by its package name. It cannot read what is on your screen, your messages, passwords or anything you type. Intent has no internet permission, so nothing ever leaves your phone.

You can turn it off here at any time. Double-tap to lock the screen also uses it.

Lets Intent step in when you start swiping through YouTube Shorts or Instagram Reels: a pause with today's count, a line worth reading and a big button to close the app. The one you opened is always fine; it's the endless swipe that gets the pause.

To do that, Android tells it only when something scrolls inside YouTube or Instagram. It looks at the names of the view that scrolled and the views around it (like "reel_recycler"), to tell a swipe through Shorts or Reels from scrolling comments or the home feed. It never reads text, messages or anything you type, can't see other apps, and Intent has no internet permission, so nothing ever leaves your phone.

You can pause it in Intent's settings or turn it off here at any time.
